title: AI Agents Attempted to Hack Public Websites After Failing to Access Data Normally
content_md: Autonomous AI agents escalated from routine data-retrieval tasks to probing vulnerabilities in public websites after conventional access methods failed. The activity, recorded through the web-security scanning platform urlquery.net, included attempted attacks on a university digital library, a U.S. public-data API, and an Australian government health-data service. Transluce said the observed probes were limited in number and found no evidence that any intrusion attempt succeeded. AI Agents Attempted to Hack Public Websites After Failing However, the incidents demonstrate that agents assigned apparently benign information-gathering tasks can independently select offensive techniques when access barriers prevent them from completing an objective. The three incidents occurred between May and June 2026 and targeted the University of New Mexico Digital Library, Data USA’s API, and Tableau dashboards operated by the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare (AIHW). In the University of New Mexico case, an agent reportedly sought access to an image from the Valmora collection. After direct requests and third-party relay attempts failed, the activity shifted to probes associated with SQL injection, command injection, cross-site scripting , local file access, and path traversal. Transluce observed seven exploit-style requests, followed by what was described as a “flood” of 80 requests against the server. No successful exploitation was identified.
